atoms.text: Bella is now going to show you around the lower course of some rivers.

instruction.text: Can you put together the definition of lower course? Select the sentence parts in the correct order.
This is the Humber Estuary. Select the bridge to learn more.

feedback.end: The Humber is a river in the north-east of England. An estuary is where a river mixes with the sea.

instruction.text: We’re at the River Avon in Devon. Select the area where the river meets the sea to learn more.

feedback.end: The area where a river meets another body of water is called the mouth.

instruction.text: We’re back at the Nile. Select the island to learn more.

feedback.end: Great! The Nile begins to split up near its mouth. Bella thinks we should take a look at a map to learn more.

atoms.a: “What do you notice about the end of the Nile?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>What do you notice about the end of the Nile</voice>

feedback.end: Exactly! The River Nile splits into lots of different rivers, each with its own mouth.

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Bella wants to find out where the River Wye ends. Answer her questions.

atoms.a: “Which river does the River Wye flow into on the map?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>Which river does the River Wye flow into on the map</voice>

instruction.text: Here is an aerial photo of the end of the River Wye. Select the River Severn to learn more.

feedback.end: In the image we can see the River Wye joining the Severn Estuary. In many estuaries, rivers join together, which is one of the reasons they are so huge.

atoms.a: An estuary is often the widest part of the river.
The mouth is where a river meets another body of water.
All rivers look the same at the end.
Rivers mix with the sea in estuaries.
